title: Performance of Western HA-VTE risk models in East Asian populations: a prospective multicenter study.
abstract: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up. The 90-day HA-VTE incidence was 2.54%. All 5 models showed moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.726-0.759). Caprini, Padua, and Intermountain models did not differ significantly (DeLong test, P> .05). Caprini had the highest sensitivity (0.83) but classified 42.6% of patients as being at high risk. Padua and Intermountain favored specificity (0.75-0.81) with lower sensitivity (0.64-0.67). Clinical model selection should align with specific balances between sensitivity and utility. In surgical inpatients, Caprini performed best (AUC, 0.804; sensitivity, 0.90; negative predictive value, 1.00), although its more than 40 input variables limit practical use. Calibration was generally acceptable. Performance varied across subgroups. The prophylaxis subgroup showed attenuated performance, with reduced discrimination (eg, Caprini AUC decreased to 0.682) and less stable calibration. Western HA-VTE models have moderate predictive value in East Asian inpatient populations. Performance differs across subgroups. Local recalibration and development of simpler, population-specific scores are needed.

title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
abstract: BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed. RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. title: Predictive value of combined cerebral blood volume index and systemic inflammation indices for 90-day functional outcomes following endovascular treatment in patients with acute ischemic stroke and proximal large vessel occlusion: machine learning model construction and population attributable fraction analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We investigated whether the cerebral blood volume (CBV) index and pretreatment systemic inflammatory indices (SIIs) provide complementary prognostic information for 90-day functional outcomes after successful endovascular therapy (EVT) for anterior circulation large vessel occlusion and evaluated the advantages of machine learning models in terms of prognostic outcomes and quantified adverse outcomes using the population attributable fraction (PAF). METHODS: This retrospective analysis of a prospective registry included 474 patients who were treated between November 2020 and June 2024. An independent 53-patient multicenter cohort was used for external validation. SIIs were calculated from the first venous sample obtained at presentation, before intravenous thrombolysis, and before arterial puncture for EVT. Multivariate logistic regression and eight predictive algorithms were evaluated. PAF estimates were considered exploratory. RESULTS: Among 474 patients, 41.6% and 28.5% achieved favorable and excellent outcomes, respectively. Higher CBV indices were more frequent among patients with favorable outcomes, whereas higher inflammatory indices were associated with worse outcomes. Logistic regression showed the highest AUC for mRS 0-2 (0.868, 95% CI 0.806-0.929), while SVM had the highest AUC for mRS 0-1 (0.839, 95% CI 0.764-0.915). The external validation AUCs were 0.816 and 0.802. PAF analysis indicated that improving the CBV index increased favorable and excellent outcomes by 97.2% and 74.8%, respectively, whereas reducing inflammatory overactivation improved them by 22.4%-39.7% and 51.2%-59.5%, respectively. CONCLUSION: Baseline CBV index and pretreatment SII values provided complementary prognostic information after successful EVT. However, prospective validation in a broader population is required before clinical implementation.

title: AI-enhanced intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery: from augmented reality navigation to foundation models.
abstract: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

title: Inferior vena cava filter-related thrombosis: Mechanisms, clinical features, prevention, diagnosis, and risk-stratified management.
abstract: Inferior vena cava (IVC) filters can provide mechanical protection from pulmonary embolism in selected patients who cannot receive anticoagulation, but filter-related thrombosis is an important complication. A uniform definition is lacking. Thrombus in the filter region may represent emboli captured by the filter, extension of pre-existing deep vein thrombosis, or local thrombus formation around the device. Filter-induced flow disturbance and vessel-wall responses may contribute to local thrombosis, although direct mechanistic evidence in humans remains limited. Reported occurrence varies substantially because study populations, imaging schedules, and outcome definitions differ. Clinically detected caval thrombosis or thrombotic occlusion is uncommon in large databases and prospective cohorts. Planned imaging before retrieval, however, often detects small intrafilter thrombi, most of which are asymptomatic. Accordingly, the clinical importance of an imaging-detected thrombus depends on whether it is accompanied by meaningful caval obstruction or symptoms. Prevention should continue throughout the filter life cycle. Filters should be used only for a time-limited, evidence-based indication. Anticoagulation should be resumed when a separate indication persists and bleeding risk permits, and retrieval should be assessed once filter-mediated pulmonary embolism protection is no longer required. Structured follow-up can help prevent loss to care. Management of established thrombosis should be guided by symptoms, impaired caval outflow, thrombus progression and chronicity, bleeding risk, and the need for filter retrieval. Anticoagulation remains foundational when indicated for active venous thromboembolism. Catheter-directed thrombolysis, mechanical thrombectomy, or combined treatment may be considered for selected symptomatic, progressive, or obstructive cases, but most supporting studies are nonrandomized. Future studies require standardized minimum reporting and patient-centered outcomes.

title: Post Hoc Association Between Intramuscular Injection Site and Ulcer Healing in Patients with Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Treated with Recombinant Human Hepatocyte Growth Factor Naked Plasmid: AAnalysis of the HOPE CLTI-2 Trial.
abstract: post hoc p p p p p p p p This study was based on the multicenter, double-blind, randomized phase III HOPE CLTI-2 trial. An exploratoryanalysis was performed to investigate the association between intramuscular injection site and ulcer healing outcomes in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) treated with recombinant human hepatocyte growth factor (rh-HGF), and to explore factors associated with ulcer healing. The analysis included 108 patients with CLTI treated with rh-HGF, comprising 184 ischemic lower-limb ulcers. Patients were classified according to injection site into a single-segment group, with injections limited to the calf muscles, and a multi-segment group, with injections administered to both the thigh and calf muscles. Outcomes included ulcer healing rate, time to ulcer healing, ankle-brachial index (ABI), Rutherford category, Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection (WIfI) classification, and adverse clinical events. At the study endpoint, the unadjusted ulcer healing rate was significantly higher in the single-segment group than in the multi-segment group (75.0% vs. 57.1%,= 0.014), and the observed time to ulcer healing was shorter (153.00 [91.00-184.00] days vs. 181.00 [94.00-191.00] days,= 0.022). No significant between-group differences were observed in changes in ABI (= 0.290) or in WIfI classification (= 0.407). However, the distribution of Rutherford categories at study endpoint favored the single-segment group (= 0.016). In the multivariable logistic regression analysis, baseline ulcer area (odds ratio [OR]: 0.684, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.519-0.901,= 0.007) and male sex (OR: 3.924, 95% CI: 1.164-13.232,= 0.028) were independently associated with ulcer healing. Although the unadjusted comparisons favored the single-segment group, injection site was not independently associated with ulcer healing after multivariable adjustment (OR: 1.560, 95% CI: 0.703-3.460,= 0.269). Therefore, these findings should be considered hypothesis-generating. Whether a more anatomically targeted rh-HGF injection strategy under a fixed-dose regimen can improve ulcer healing requires evaluation in prospectively designed studies.

title: Cause-Specific Endovascular Thrombectomy Time Windows in Basilar Artery Occlusion: ATTENTION Trial Post Hoc Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) outperforms best medical treatment (BMT) for basilar artery occlusion (BAO), but the influence of stroke cause on the time sensitivity of EVT remains unclear. We hypothesized nonatherosclerotic BAO would require earlier EVT, whereas atherosclerotic BAO-with chronic stenosis and more robust collaterals-would retain EVT benefit in extended windows. We conducted a post hoc 3-way interaction analysis of the ATTENTION trial (Trial of Endovascular Treatment of Acute Basilar Artery Occlusion) to explore cause-specific EVT time patterns. METHODS: Using randomized ATTENTION trial data (36 Chinese centers, 2021-2022), patients were stratified by onset-to-puncture time (<6 versus ≥6 hours) and TOAST (Trial of ORG 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment) cause (atherosclerotic: large-artery atherosclerosis; nonatherosclerotic: cardioembolism/undetermined/other causes). The primary outcome was 90-day favorable functional outcome (modified Rankin Scale score 0-3), with relative risk as the primary estimand; the 3-way interaction was tested via joint Wald test. A weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis served as an exploratory tool, with multivariable regression adjusting for confounders. RESULTS: P P P P P P Among 340 patients (226 EVT+BMT, 114 BMT), for onset-to-puncture time <6 hours, patients without atherosclerosis with EVT achieved a significantly higher favorable outcome rate (46.7% versus 20.4%; relative risk, 2.29 [95% CI, 1.25-4.18];=0.007); patients with atherosclerosis showed numerical outcome benefit (40.4% versus 26.1%,=0.259). For onset-to-puncture time ≥6 hours, numerical benefit of patients with atherosclerosis increased from 14.3% to 30.6% (56.9% versus 26.3%;=0.199), accompanied by ordinal modified Rankin Scale score improvement (common odds ratio, 3.30 [95% CI, 1.13-9.62];=0.029) and National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score reduction; patients without atherosclerosis' benefit decreased from 26.3% to 17.8% with loss of significance (39.5% versus 21.7%,=0.341). The treatment time×cause interaction was not significant (=0.662). The weighted 1-hour interval odds ratio trend analysis identified a provisional 5.3-hour reference point in patients without atherosclerosis. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with nonatherosclerotic BAO, atherosclerotic BAO appears less time-sensitive, potentially retaining EVT responsiveness over longer windows. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation. REGISTRATION: URL: https://www.clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT04751708.

title: Long-term outcome of stenting for the iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral arterio-venous graft; a case series.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To analyze the possible etiology and evaluate the technical and clinical outcomes of using bare metal stents for the treatment of central venous stenosis (CVS) in the lower extremity with ipsilateral hemodialysis access. METHODS: A single-center retrospective analysis of a small case series was conducted in hemodialysis patients with lower extremity arteriovenous grafts (AVG) who were treated with bare metal stents (BMS) for symptomatic iliac vein stenosis between April 2016 and June 2021. Patients' demographic data, technical details, adverse events, clinical outcomes, and imaging data were recorded. RESULTS: The study cohort comprised seven females and four males, with a mean age of 58.8 ± 13.4 years. Preoperative lower limb venography was performed in nine patients scheduled for AVG creation. With the exception of one case demonstrating left iliac vein compression, the iliac veins were patent in all other patients. Symptoms of lower limb swelling developed at a mean interval of 9.40 ± 5.83 months (range: 3-20 months) following AVG placement. Eight cases had a concomitant history of temporary ipsilateral femoral vein catheterization. Lesion characteristics included nine stenotic lesions and two occlusive lesions. All patients were treated with SMART Control stents (Cordis Corp, USA). The technical success rate was 100%, and symptomatic relief was achieved in all cases. Over a mean follow-up period of 47.8 ± 31.7 months (range: 10-123 months), the target lesion primary patency was 100% (one-side confidence interval [CI] = 0.74,1). CONCLUSIONS: Using BMS is a safe and effective method to treat iliac vein stenosis with ipsilateral AVG.

title: Bilateral peripheral CT venography for evaluating central venous lesions in dysfunctional arteriovenous fistulas: feasibility, safety, and radiation dose in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Central venous stenosis and occlusion are major causes of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) dysfunction in hemodialysis patients. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility, safety, radiation exposure, and anatomical findings of bilateral peripheral CT venography for central venous assessment in patients with dysfunctional AVFs. METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort study included 46 consecutive hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs who underwent bilateral peripheral CT venography between August 2023 and June 2025. Technical success, procedure-related adverse events, radiation dose parameters, central venous lesion characteristics, and agreement with available comparative imaging modalities were analyzed. Comparative imaging findings from puncture-based angiography and/or duplex ultrasonography were assessed descriptively. RESULTS: All 46 examinations were technically successful (100%), with a mean procedure duration of 4 minutes (range, 3-5 minutes). Minor adverse events included one patient of contrast extravasation (2.2%) and 3 of mild allergic reactions (6.5%); no severe procedure-related complications were documented. The mean CTDIvol and DLP were 11.87 mGy and 784.15 mGy·cm, respectively. Central venous abnormalities were identified in 44 patients (95.7%), including stenosis in 31 (67.4%), occlusion in 11 (23.9%), and aneurysmal changes in 2 (4.3%). Comparative imaging was available in 38 patients, and CT venography showed agreement with available findings in 37 cases (97.4%). This agreement was interpreted as descriptive concordance rather than formal diagnostic accuracy. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral peripheral CT venography demonstrated high technical feasibility, acceptable safety, and effective visualization of central venous abnormalities in hemodialysis patients with dysfunctional AVFs. Further prospective studies are needed to validate its diagnostic performance and clinical impact. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This technique enables efficient, noninvasive assessment of central venous pathology with minimal risk, supporting its potential as a practical alternative to conventional imaging in hemodialysis patients.

title: Delayed deterioration after surgical treatment of a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula detected by three spinal angiographies: Case report.
abstract: Spinal dural arteriovenous fistulas (DAVFs) are the most common subtype of spinal arteriovenous malformations, and they often cause progressive myelopathy. Early detection and intervention are critical to preventing irreversible neurological deficits. Selective spinal angiography remains the gold standard for diagnosing this condition. However, for some patients with typical clinical features and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) findings consistent with DAVF, the initial angiography may fail to detect the lesion. In this article, we report a case of T4 low-flow spinal DAVF that was only identified after three rounds of spinal angiography. The fistula was successfully occluded via surgery, and the patient's symptoms gradually improved postoperatively. Nevertheless, the patient later developed recurrent, aggravated symptoms. The delayed deterioration of previously resolved symptoms was attributed to venous thrombosis, and the condition improved after systemic anticoagulation therapy with heparin. The patients fluctuating symptoms stabilized one month after combined therapy with anticoagulants and antiplatelet drugs. For patients with a high clinical suspicion of spinal DAVF, required to confirm the final diagnosis. Delayed deterioration can occur secondary to progressive venous thrombosis, so preventive anticoagulation is indicated for selected patient's, and this intervention should be individualized.

title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

title: Analysis of risk factors and construction of a prediction model for postoperative deep vein thrombosis in patients with periarticular knee fractures.
abstract: The present study aimed to identify risk factors for postoperative deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients with periarticular knee fractures. A prediction model was constructed for the early identification of high-risk patients. Data from 319 patients at who underwent surgery at the Affiliated Hospital of Southwest Medical University (Luzhou, China) between January 2020 and December 2022 were analyzed. Based on ultrasound results, patients were divided into a DVT group (n=83) and a non-DVT group (n=236). Logistic regression was employed to identify independent risk factors. Subsequently, a nomogram model was established, which was validated via receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The DVT rate was 26.0%. Old age (OR, 1.0228), high American Society of Anesthesiologists grade (OR, 2.2764), greater blood loss (OR, 1.0015), blood transfusion (OR, 2.7917) and high D-dimer levels (OR, 1.0251) were identified as independent risk factors (P<0.05), while living in cities, high hemoglobin, high prealbumin, high Barthel index and high Braden scores served as protective factors (P<0.05). The model yielded an area under the curve value of 0.837. Additionally, the calibration curve showed high accuracy, and DCA validated the favorable clinical applicability of this predictive model. In conclusion, the model performs well in helping doctors to identify high-risk patients and optimize individualized therapeutic strategies.

title: Duplex ultrasound as an initial imaging clue to spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection: A case report.
abstract: Spontaneous isolated celiac artery dissection is uncommon and is usually confirmed with computed tomography angiography (CTA). Duplex ultrasound may provide an initial clue when the lesion and its flow abnormalities are directly visualized. A 56-year-old woman with untreated hypertension presented with acute persistent epigastric pain radiating to the back. Color Doppler ultrasound at the celiac artery origin demonstrated an intimal flap separating the true and false lumens, with an adjacent hypoechoic component without detectable flow. Spectral Doppler sampling within the dissected segment showed a peak systolic velocity of 225 cm/s with spectral broadening. Initial CTA confirmed proximal celiac artery dissection. On short-interval repeat imaging, the maximum outer diameter at the same anatomic level increased from 8.8 mm to 9.7 mm, the true lumen became more compressed, and new false-lumen thrombosis appeared. Symptoms had not progressed; the decision to intervene was driven by imaging progression. False-lumen coil embolization and stent placement were performed. Follow-up CTA demonstrated a patent stent, preserved major branch perfusion, and no residual false-lumen opacification. In this patient, duplex ultrasound provided an initial imaging clue, whereas CTA confirmed the diagnosis, documented interval remodeling, and assessed the post-treatment anatomy.

title: High BMI-attributable burden of eight diseases relevant to the CKM framework in China: GBD 2023 estimates and projections to 2050.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome is a recently defined clinical entity integrating metabolic risk factors, chronic kidney disease, and cardiovascular disease. Elevated body mass index (BMI) is a major modifiable risk factor for CKM syndrome, yet comprehensive long-term analyses of the high BMI-attributable burden in China remain scarce. METHODS: Using data from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2023 study, we assessed the burden of eight selected CKM-related diseases attributable to high BMI (atrial fibrillation and flutter [AFF], chronic kidney disease due to hypertension [CKD-HTN] or diabetes mellitus type 2 [CKD-T2DM], diabetes mellitus type 2 [T2DM], hypertensive heart disease [HHD], ischemic heart disease [IHD], lower extremity peripheral arterial disease [LEPAD], and stroke) in China from 1990 to 2023. The primary outcomes were absolute deaths and DALYs and their age-standardized rates (ASRs) per 100,000 population. Joinpoint regression and ARIMA models were applied to analyze and project temporal trends in ASRs, age-period-cohort analysis was conducted using age-specific rates, and decomposition analysis quantified the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological change to changes in absolute deaths and DALYs. RESULTS: From 1990 to 2023, absolute deaths and DALYs for all eight selected diseases relevant to the CKM framework increased. IHD had the highest burden in 2023 (114,980 deaths; 2,923,595 DALYs), whereas AFF showed the greatest relative increase (11.4-fold). Descriptively, men generally had higher point estimates of death and DALY counts, ASMRs, and ASDRs for CKD-T2DM, CKD-HTN, IHD, and HHD, whereas women had higher corresponding estimates for AFF. Joinpoint regression identified sustained increases in AFF, IHD, T2DM, and LEPAD, with several inflection points around 2005. APC analysis showed pronounced age-related gradients and variations in period and cohort rate ratios. Decomposition analysis indicated that population aging was the predominant contributor to increasing mortality for most outcomes, while epidemiological change had heterogeneous effects and partially offset increases in CKD-T2DM and HHD. Model-based projections suggested heterogeneous future trajectories: increasing mortality and DALY rates for AFF, IHD, and LEPAD; increasing DALYs but slightly declining mortality for T2DM; broadly stable or slightly declining rates for stroke, CKD-T2DM, and CKD-HTN; and declining point estimates for HHD, although with substantial long-term uncertainty. CONCLUSION: High BMI-attributable stage 2-4 CKM burden has risen sharply in China and will continue to increase, driven mainly by worsening epidemiological risks. AFF, IHD, and LEPAD show the fastest growth. Men had higher age-standardized mortality and DALY rates for several selected diseases. Early-life obesity prevention and sex-tailored interventions are urgently needed.

title: Hybrid pin penetration open stent technique: Retrospective study of a new approach to frozen elephant trunk procedure.
abstract: Total arch replacement using the frozen elephant trunk technique for acute type A aortic dissection involving the aortic arch remains technically demanding because of complex supra-aortic branch reconstruction and prolonged circulatory arrest. We developed a modified fenestrated open stent technique, termed the hybrid pin-penetration open stent (HIPPOS) technique, to simplify branch reconstruction while minimizing supra-aortic vessel manipulation. We retrospectively reviewed 15 consecutive patients who underwent total arch replacement using HIPPOS between May 2024 and May 2026 at a single institution by a single surgeon. Following deployment of a Frozenix open stent graft (Japan Lifeline), antegrade fenestrations were created under direct vision using needle penetration and sequential dilation, followed by reconstruction with balloon-expandable covered stent grafts. All procedures were successfully completed. Operative durations decreased with increasing numbers of fenestrations, reflecting procedural refinement and the surgical learning curve. Two perioperative deaths occurred in patients with profound preoperative shock, and one patient experienced a nondisabling stroke. No postoperative hoarseness, paraplegia, fenestration-related endoleak, or distal stent-induced new entry was observed. Follow-up computed tomography angiography confirmed satisfactory graft conformability and durable branch patency. HIPPOS is a reproducible modification of the frozen elephant trunk procedure with encouraging early clinical outcomes.

title: Incidence, Risk Factors, and Outcomes of Early Post-Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt Hyperbilirubinemia.
abstract: PURPOSE: To determine the incidence, risk factors, and outcomes of early post-transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) hyperbilirubinemia in cirrhotic patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, 1,404 cirrhotic patients who underwent TIPS were analyzed. Patients with early post-TIPS hyperbilirubinemia (total bilirubin [TB] ≥ 5 mg/dL within 1 week after TIPS; primary predictor) were classified as Group A, and those without it were classified as Group B. Threshold effect analysis was used to identify the optimal cutoff for the change in TB (exploratory parameter), followed by Fine-Gray modeling. RESULTS: Early post-TIPS hyperbilirubinemia occurred in 67 patients (4.8%). The cumulative incidence of mortality was higher in Group A than in Group B at 1 year (37.3% vs 7.7%), 3 years (49.7% vs 19.8%), and 5 years (49.7% vs 30.3%; P < .001). Multivariate analysis identified early post-TIPS hyperbilirubinemia (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR], 3.03; P < .001), age (sHR, 1.05; P < .001), albumin level (sHR, 0.96; P < .001), model for end-stage liver disease score (sHR, 1.05; P = .005), and hepatocellular carcinoma (sHR, 1.77; P < .001) as independent predictors of mortality. Change in TB was independently associated with mortality whether analyzed as a continuous variable (sHR, 1.19; P < .001) or dichotomized at 2.98 mg/dL (sHR, 2.64; P < .001). Rounding the cutoff to 3 mg/dL did not materially alter the association (sHR, 2.58; P < .001). CONCLUSION: TB ≥ 5 mg/dL within the first week after TIPS, or ΔTB ≥ 2.98mg/dL (∼3 mg/dL) was independently associated with mortality.

title: Deep learning versus radiologists for acute aortic dissection on CT: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract: Acute aortic dissection (AAD) is a time-sensitive cardiovascular emergency in which delayed recognition remains associated with poor early outcomes, and deep learning (DL) applied to computed tomography (CT) is increasingly proposed for triage support. We synthesized DL detection accuracy on CT, compared DL with radiologists head-to-head, and secondarily pooled CT segmentation accuracy. This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-compliant review searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science through February 18, 2026. Detection studies were pooled with bivariate random-effects models; head-to-head comparisons were synthesized with contrast-based network meta-analysis; segmentation Sørensen-Dice coefficients were analyzed with three-level random-effects models. Twenty-three studies were included. For non-contrast CT detection (10 studies; 18 cohorts; 54 algorithm-cohort datasets), pooled sensitivity was 0.91 (95 % confidence interval [CI], 0.87-0.94) and specificity 0.90 (95 % CI, 0.85-0.94). In direct comparisons (5 studies; 11 comparisons), radiologist-to-DL relative sensitivity was 0.72 (95 % CI, 0.57-0.91) and relative specificity 0.88 (95 % CI, 0.83-0.93). For the secondary segmentation synthesis (16 studies; 88 datasets), pooled Dice was 0.863 (95 % CI, 0.795-0.931), lower for true- and false-lumen than for whole-aorta delineation. DL showed encouraging detection accuracy and higher sensitivity and specificity than the radiologist comparators in five head-to-head studies read under experimental conditions, supporting assistive triage rather than replacement; lumen-level segmentation remains more challenging than whole-aorta contouring. Certainty was low - datasets were predominantly case-control with a median prevalence of 50 %, heterogeneity was substantial and small-study effects pronounced - so these estimates are experimental upper bounds requiring prospective confirmation.

title: Risk Factors for Deep Vein Thrombosis After Surgery in Patients with Gastric or Colorectal Cancer Receiving Anticoagulant Prophylaxis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Our objective was to identify perioperative predictors of early postoperative lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) in patients undergoing surgery for gastric or colorectal cancer who received routine pharmacologic thromboprophylaxis and to develop a nomogram for postoperative risk stratification. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients with gastric or colorectal cancer undergoing surgery from December 2020 to October 2023. All received postoperative low-molecular-weight heparin prophylaxis, and DVT was screened by ultrasonography on postoperative day 3. Predictors were identified by logistic regression and incorporated into a nomogram. RESULTS: A total of 388 eligible patients were included, among whom 124 (32.0%) had screening-detected postoperative lower-extremity DVT. Among patients with DVT, 118 (95.2%) had distal-only DVT and 114 (91.9%) were asymptomatic. Multivariable logistic regression identified age, activated partial thromboplastin time, prothrombin time, and postoperative day 1 D-dimer as independent predictors of postoperative DVT. The nomogram showed acceptable discrimination, with area under the receiver operating characteristic curve values of 0.787 (95% confidence interval 0.731-0.844) in the training cohort and 0.854 (95% confidence interval 0.774-0.934) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed good agreement between predicted and observed risks. In decision curve analysis, the nomogram provided greater net benefit for risk classification than strategies classifying all or no patients as high risk. CONCLUSION: Age, activated partial thromboplastin time, prothrombin time, and postoperative day 1 D-dimer were independently associated with screening-detected early postoperative DVT. The resulting nomogram may help postoperative risk stratification and closer surveillance; however, external validation is required before routine clinical application.

abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the prognostic value of early psoas muscle index (PMI) improvement after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) placement in patients with cirrhosis and sarcopenia. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 2 2 2 2 This multicenter retrospective study included 390 patients with cirrhosis and sarcopenia who underwent TIPS at 5 tertiary centers between February 2016 and April 2023. PMI was measured on computed tomography (CT) before TIPS and ∼1 month afterward. Sarcopenia reversal was defined as a post-TIPS PMI above the sex-specific cutoff values (>6.36 cm/mfor men and >3.92 cm/mfor women). Associations of PMI improvement with overall survival and overt hepatic encephalopathy (OHE) were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis identified optimal cutoff values. RESULTS: At 1 month after TIPS, 188 patients (48.2%) achieved sarcopenia reversal. Sarcopenia reversal was associated with higher cumulative survival (84.6% vs 68.2%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.24; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.14-0.41; P < .001) and lower OHE incidence (16.6% vs 51.1%; HR, 0.26; 95% CI, 0.17-0.39; P < .001). The PMI improvement rate was an independent predictor of mortality and OHE. Optimal cutoff values were 11.8% for mortality and 15.8% for OHE. Patients with PMI improvement above these thresholds had significantly better survival and lower OHE incidence (both P < .001). CONCLUSIONS: PMI improvement assessed at 1 month after TIPS is independently associated with reduced mortality and OHE in patients with cirrhosis and sarcopenia. PMI assessment 1 month after TIPS may provide a simple imaging biomarker for early prognostic evaluation and risk stratification.

title: Drug-Eluting Stents versus Drug-Coated Balloons Plus Bare-Metal Stents for the Treatment of Femoropopliteal Artery Lesions: 2-Year Outcomes from the TALENT Study.
abstract: PURPOSE: To compare the 2-year outcomes of drug-eluting stents (DES) versus drug-coated balloons (DCB) plus bare-metal stents (BMS) in patients with femoropopliteal artery disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Data were analyzed from The Impact of Tibial Runoff on Clinical Outcome of Endovascular Therapy in Femoropopliteal Lesions (TALENT) study, a multicenter, prospective study. Inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to balance baseline characteristics. The primary outcomes were freedom of all-cause mortality, freedom of major adverse events, clinically driven target lesion revascularization (CD-TLR), and major adverse limb events (MALEs), and the secondary outcomes were the improvement in Rutherford classification and changes in quality of life assessed by the 25-item Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire. RESULTS: A total of 429 patients were included (81 in DES group; 348 in DCB plus BMS group). During a median (Q1-Q3) follow-up of 20.2 months (11.6-27.1 months), no significant differences were observed between the 2 groups in 2-year freedom of all-cause mortality (91.4% vs 85.1%; P = .096), freedom of major adverse events (79.6% vs 73.9%; P = .330), CD-TLR (9.6% vs 12.6%; P = .737), and MALEs (10.1% vs 12.3%; P = .612). Both treatment modalities significantly improved in VascuQol score and Rutherford classification, with improvement rates of 76.1% and 71.3% at 24 months, respectively. An interaction effect (P = .014 and .005, respectively) was observed for patients with intermittent claudication (R2-R3), suggesting that DES may be associated with lower risks of CD-TLR and MALEs. CONCLUSIONS: Over the 2-year follow-up, DES and DCB plus BMS demonstrated favorable and comparable overall effectiveness in real-world patients with complex femoropopliteal lesions.

title: MitraNav: Design and Modeling of a Robotic System for Transseptal Mitral Valve Replacement with Dock Catheter Task-Space Control.
abstract: PURPOSE: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is a promising therapy for reducing mitral regurgitation in select patients. Direct tip control of multi-segment catheters can simplify manipulation and enable precise, stable positioning. This paper introduces MitraNav, the first robotic system developed for dock-based TMVR, focusing on system design and task-space control of the dock catheter. METHODS: Built on a previously validated guide-sheath robot, MitraNav is upgraded to support concentric multi-catheter manipulation via a unified actuation mechanism. It suits both dock and balloon catheters, enabling all catheter manipulation using a single robotic system. A two-segment bending model maps joint space to task space through an intermediate configuration space. A two-stage control strategy is then applied: joint-space control allows for rapid approach to the mitral annulus, followed by task-space control for direct tip positioning. To improve accuracy and handle joint limits, the task-space controller incorporates Jacobian normalization to balance joint contributions, null-space optimization to regulate joint motion without affecting the primary task, and a PD controller to reduce tracking errors. RESULTS: Trajectory-following experiments demonstrate feasibility of direct tip control, with maximum errors of 2.38 mm, 2.53 mm, and 2.46 mm in three trials. These positional errors are within the range of acceptable accuracy commonly considered for catheter-based cardiac interventions. CONCLUSION: MitraNav represents the foundation for intuitive catheter manipulation and offers the potential for semi-autonomous robotic dock-based TMVR.

title: Influence of Hypertension on the Regional Elastic Properties of Ascending Thoracic Aortic Aneurysms with Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
abstract: Although hypertension may affect the local biomechanical properties of ascending thoracic aortic aneurysms (ATAAs) with a bicuspid aortic valve (BAV), a comparison of the regional elastic properties of BAV-ATAAs between patients with and without hypertension is not yet available due to lack of biomechanical data. In this study, we collected 25 fresh ATAA samples from 17 hypertensive and 8 age-matched non-hypertensive patients who underwent elective aortic surgery. Biomechanical tests were executed to investigate the regional failure stresses and biaxial mechanical properties of BAV-ATAAs with and without hypertension. A material model was fitted to the biaxial experimental data to obtain model parameters in different regions. Histological analysis was performed to investigate the underlying microstructure and determine the percentages of elastic and collagen fibers. The circumferential failure stresses in the anterior, lateral, and posterior regions were significantly lower for the hypertensive group than in the non-hypertensive group. Regarding equibiaxial stresses, the hypertensive BAV-ATAAs showed significantly higher longitudinal tissue stiffness in the anterior and lateral regions than the non-hypertensive BAV-ATAAs. Collagen fiber hyperplasia was observed in the anterior and lateral regions of both the hypertensive and non-hypertensive BAV-ATAAs. However, in these regions the laminar structure of the elastic fibers was disrupted in several places and apoptotic smooth muscle cells were observed in the group with hypertension compared to the group without hypertension. In addition, the circumferential failure stresses in the anterior and lateral regions were significantly increased in the hypertensive group and strongly correlated with the collagen content. These results suggest that the regional elastic properties of the hypertensive BAV-ATAAs are more deteriorated than those of the non-hypertensive samples. Due to the significant impact on circumferential tensile strength, the hypertensive BAV patients may be at a higher risk of ATAA rupture than non-hypertensive BAV patients.
